snp5.14:3.3: This state of mind matches the five-factored noble right concentration described in AN 5:28 and analyzed further in AN 9:36. See also section III/F of The Wings to Awakening, and the essays “Jhāna Not by the Numbers” and “Silence Isn’t Mandatory.”
snp5.14:3.4: AN 3:33 discusses this verse. There the Buddha tells Ven. Sāriputta to train so that, with regard to this conscious body and to all external objects of concentration alike, there’s no “I”-making, “mine”-making, or underlying conceit, and so that one enters and remains in the awareness-release and discernment-release free of such “I”-making, “mine”-making, and conceit. Having trained this way, the Buddha says, one is said to have cut through craving, unraveled the fetter, and — through rightly penetrating conceit — put an end to suffering; it was with this state in mind, he adds, that he spoke this verse.
snp5.14:7.4: See DN 11, DN 15, MN 49, and SN 12:67. On “bringing consciousness to a halt” as the ending of its proliferating activity rather than an annihilation of consciousness itself, see SN 22:53; see also the simile at SN 12:64.
